messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a spike of login failures and subsequent account lockouts that looks correlated with a service account token refresh storm. ~120 lockouts across several teams in the last 10m. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/observability/auth/alerts/xyz

maria: Sample auth log snippets below, looks like mixed geo hits and a high rate of MFA challenges for the same service principal: 
```
2024-06-15T14:02:11Z auth.sso svc=svc-ingest-prod src_ip=185.45.23.10 geo=DE result=challenge_mfa
2024-06-15T14:02:12Z auth.sso svc=svc-ingest-prod src_ip=3.8.2.11 geo=US result=challenge_mfa
2024-06-15T14:02:13Z auth.sso user=alice@example.com src_ip=3.8.2.12 geo=US result=locked
2024-06-15T14:03:01Z auth.audit svc=svc-ingest-prod action=refresh_token token_kid=KID-27 result=200
```

aj: Ack. I'm on it. Any idea if this is an exploited credential or misconfigured client?

maria: Not sure yet. The svc account is allowed interactive auth currently (legacy). I suspect a refresh loop from a new deploy that still does interactive refresh.

lee: If svc account shouldn't be interactive we should immediately block interactive logins for it and rotate any long-lived tokens. Can someone run a session revoke and add a temporary deny rule in auth gateway?

maria: On it. Running: `authctl sessions revoke --principal svc-ingest-prod --reason "automated refresh storm"` and adding short-lived deny via `authctl policy patch` now.

security-oncall-bot: ALERT id=auth-wave-20240615 severity=high detections=120 affected_users=svc-ingest-prod, multiple human users; rule=improbable_login_pattern; suggested_action=contain

zoe: Also check KMS access logs for key usage spikes tied to that svc principal. If it's using KMS unattended rotation, we need to see if KMS keys were exfiltrated or mis-scoped.

maria: KMS logs show frequent decrypt operations from svc-ingest-prod key=projects/redwood/keys/ingest-key starting at 2024-06-15T13:58Z. Not seeing obvious anomalies in KMS response codes yet.

aj: Good. For immediate containment: 1) revoke sessions (done) 2) block the src IP ranges we saw 3) add a temporary rate-limit on token refresh endpoints 4) rotate the service account keys and reduce scopes. Lee, can you take 2 & 3?

lee: Adding CIDR blocks to deny-list now: 185.45.23.0/24 and 3.8.2.0/24. Applying rate-limit: `gatewayctl limit create --route /auth/refresh --key principal:svc-ingest-prod --rps 1`

maria: Keys rotated for svc-ingest-prod and old KID-27 revoked. Created new KID-98 and pushed rotated creds to vault (vault ticket #INC-2451).

zoe: I'll pull audit logs for the last 24h across auth, KMS, and vault to look for lateral activity and any unusual principal delegation. Also will check RBAC for any broad groups that include svc-ingest-prod.

sre-bot: deploybot: noticed a config change to ingestion service 2024-06-15T13:55 — env var USE_REFRESH_LOOP=true in canary. Author: @sam.

maria: That matches the timeline. Likely a canary that enabled a bad refresh loop. Sam team, can you roll back the canary?

lee: Sam, please rollback or patch client to use proper token refresh backoff. Until then we keep deny rules and rate limit in place.

aj: Next steps (post-incident): - Enforce non-interactive flag on service accounts by default - Add automated RBAC check that flags principal with login permissions + long-lived keys - Improve KMS audit retention and alerting on key use anomalies - Add integration test to catch refresh-loop misconfig in CI

maria: Agreed. I'll file follow-up tasks: TICKET-SEC-1022 (RBAC default change), TICKET-SEC-1023 (KMS alerting), TICKET-SEC-1024 (CI check). Also recommending we notify affected humans (alice, bob) about unlock & MFA fatigue and provide support.

zoe: Will gather logs and write a short timeline for postmortem. Can someone save the revoked key KID-27 metadata and the deny policy snapshot to the incident bundle?

maria: Done. Uploaded artifacts to: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2451/artifacts (deny_policy.json, revoked_keys.csv, auth_logs_20240615.zip)

lee: Monitor is green for the last 5m, lockouts down to baseline. Removing temporary IP deny in 30m if no regression.

aj: Thanks team. We'll schedule a 30m sync to finalize comms and assign owners for the post-incident tickets. :thumbsup:
